newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Tuesday, with most early-maturing contracts pushed up by institutions speculating on the rising domestic A share market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.80 percent from 11.70 percent on Monday.
Turnover fell to 5.01 million lots from 9.08 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Shanghai's A share index rose 0.96 percent today.
"If the A market continues to rise in the next few days, the early-maturing contracts will go up," one trader said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Tuesday and prices moved in a narrow range in dull trading, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 ended little changed at 122.30 yuan from 122.28 yuan. Combined volume of the eight-contract market rose to 993,547 lots from 587,181 lots.
Traders believe the contracts will continue to consolidate in a narrow range in the short term.
